title: Consistent API error responses
when: An HTTP API returns errors in mixed shapes (strings, stack traces, 200 with error) and clients cannot handle them reliably.
prompt:
Goal: Every error response has the right status and the same JSON shape with a stable code, a readable message and field details.
Steps:
1. Adopt one shape, close to RFC 9457 problem details: { "type", "title", "status", "detail", "code", "errors": [{ "field", "message" }] }.
2. Send it with Content-Type: application/problem+json or application/json, consistently.
3. Define stable machine codes (VALIDATION_FAILED, NOT_FOUND, RATE_LIMITED) that clients branch on.
4. Funnel every failure through one sendError(res, status, code, detail, errors) helper and one catch all for unexpected errors (500 with a generic message).
5. Include a requestId so users can report it; keep stacks and internals in server logs only.
6. Add Retry-After to 429 and 503 responses.
Quality bar:
- Clients can switch on code without parsing messages.
- Validation errors list every bad field at once.
- No internal details leak.
Pitfalls:
- Different shapes per route.
- Throwing raw errors that print the stack to the client.
- Using 500 for client mistakes.
Verify:
- [ ] Every error path uses the helper.
- [ ] Status codes match the case.
- [ ] Responses declare JSON content type.
- [ ] Unknown routes return 404 in the same shape.
Output: errors.js with sendError and codes, and routes updated to use it.

examples.input: cada rota devolve erro de um jeito diferente
examples.output: sendError with { status, code, title, detail, errors }, 422 lists fields, 500 generic with requestId
